doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Playing for Governor Faubus then Harlem: tunes in two and in four
summary: The Woody Herman band played in two for a politicians' party, then in four two days later in Harlem.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I was reading Woody Herman Chronicle of the Herds book and there was an interesting anecdote from you talking about in two days, one day you’re playing for Governor Faubus of Arkansas and the next night you’re playing in Harlem.
Can you tell me a little bit about that?
Yes. We went down, wasn’t that Governor Faubus —

Alabama. Well we started playing in the beginning, people just coming into the room, right? [sings] “It was just one of those things,” sounds like a general business band except it was written by Ralph Burns. But we were getting away with it only everything’s in two, right? And the second set comes by and we’re still in two — we take a break, we come back and we’re in two. By now these old politicians and whatever they are, are getting a little juiced and they’re feeling no pain. Then we go to four. Now when we went to Harlem, two days later, we just started right out in four. We didn’t mess around.
